_meta.description: Campaign ledger and measurement schema (owner brief, Priority 4 and the measurement paragraph). The ledger starts empty and stays empty until rows are obtained from authorized first-party reports. No conversion score or revenue forecast is presented anywhere in this repository, and none may be derived from this file.

columns.name: timestamp_utc
columns.meaning: When the reported period or the row's observation began, in UTC.
columns.source_required: Authorized first-party report header (Associates Central reports export, or the site's own analytics export).

columns.name: source
columns.meaning: The named first-party report the row was read from, with its report date.
columns.source_required: Associates Central report name/export file, or the local counter export file name.

columns.name: channel
columns.meaning: Where the measured session came from (for example organic search, direct, feed).
columns.source_required: The report's own channel breakdown; left blank if the report does not split channels.

columns.name: eligible_sessions
columns.meaning: Sessions eligible for attribution in the period, as the report counts them.

columns.name: clicks
columns.meaning: Outbound product-link clicks (event: outbound_click) or reported Special Link clicks (event: reported_click), as named in the source column.
columns.source_required: Local counter export (site-side) or Associates Central reports export (report-side).

columns.name: reported_orders
columns.meaning: Orders the report attributes to Special Links in the period (event: reported_order).

_meta.provenance_rule: Every row must name the authorized first-party report it came from and the date that report was read. Rows without a named first-party source are refused. Invented, modelled or synthetic values are refused (engine.tracking rejects source='synthetic-example'; see ENGINE.md). Keep a dated provenance trail: the source column is part of the row, not a footnote.

events.note: The brief asks to 'record the five defined events' but no earlier definition of those events exists in this repository (flag F-58). The five events are defined here (decision D-42), split between what this site can measure itself and what only an authorized first-party report can supply. The site-side events are recorded by a privacy-preserving local counter (docs/tracker.js): the visitor's own browser only, no network call, no cross-site identifier, no third-party analytics (decision D-16).

list.name: page_view
list.source_of_truth: The visitor's own browser; exportable from the Analytics page as JSON/CSV.

list.name: outbound_click
list.recorded_by: docs/tracker.js, localStorage only (no network request); fires on every product link click
list.source_of_truth: The visitor's own browser; exportable from the Analytics page as JSON/CSV.

list.name: chooser_answer
list.recorded_by: docs/tracker.js, localStorage only (no network request); fires on the three-question chooser
list.source_of_truth: The visitor's own browser; exportable from the Analytics page as JSON/CSV.

list.name: reported_click
list.recorded_by: Associates Central reports export only; never generated by this site
list.source_of_truth: The authorized first-party Associates report named in the ledger row's source column.

list.name: reported_order
list.recorded_by: Associates Central reports export only; never generated by this site
list.source_of_truth: The authorized first-party Associates report named in the ledger row's source column.

endpoint.status: Not configured. GitHub Pages serves static files only, so no self-hosted analytics endpoint exists yet (decision D-44). The local counter exports a standard payload from the Analytics page; the owner can post that payload to a self-hosted endpoint once one is provisioned and its privacy/consent basis is settled (Q-49, Q-17). Nothing is sent anywhere in the meantime.
